fixtures: Keep the five three-file bugs, their initial public tests, and all 72 held-out tests per task from experiment 62. In four tasks, choose a fixed pool in an agreement region of the initially green pairs: equality for labels and net weight, above the gate for cycle offset, equal quotient and remainder for residual loading. Keep a distinguishing fixed input for paint usage as a control.
policy: Keep the same 32 single-edit and 64 pair limits in both languages and both modes. Search the same fixed pool first. In generation mode, if no distinguishing fixed point is found and the complete pair search has multiple green pairs, generate midpoints, minimums, maximums, the clamped witness, one-axis neighbors and corners. Use a separate limit of 32 distinct inputs and 128 candidate evaluations for each stage. Skip public and already tried inputs for the generated stage. Compare candidate values only when all candidates return normally.
resolution: For either mode, confirm the first disagreement with the common independent TIDE contract, append the confirmed public test, remove it from the fixed pool, and repeat under identical budgets. Allow up to three confirmations. Apply a unique pair by jointly previewing both files and writing them to a fresh scratch copy. Count unresolved work, truncation, or failed final acceptance as unsuccessful.
acceptance: Reopen the scratch project and check every public test and the unchanged 72 held-out tests. The repair commands receive the held-out cases only after the edit has been applied. Check whether generated confirmations are disjoint from held-out data after the repair.
timer: Use a monotonic wall clock, from before fixed-pool creation to acceptance or abstention. Include all process starts, generation, confirmation, repeated filtering, patch previews, source writes and final tests. Report successful repair times and time to abstention separately.
repetitions: Twelve timed pairs per task and mode after dry verification. Interleave fixed-only and generation modes, rotate the tasks and alternate language precedence. Fresh CLI processes and scratch copies, one logical CPU, warm file caches. All attempts are local, with no model requests.
